data.why: the repo ships a real spectrum photo in web/samples/sample.jpg for upload testing, and the in-page 'load example' button also synthesizes a known spectrum entirely client-side

goals: upload a photo of a diffraction/grating spectrum and automatically detect spectral line positions
calibrate pixel position to wavelength using a reference lamp (Hg/Na/H/He) or manual two-point entry
identify which of the 12 library elements are present from the matched line wavelengths
compute the grating constant d = k*lambda/sin(theta) with propagated uncertainty from vernier angle readings
export the line table and calibration results as CSV/JSON and generate a printable report

review.summary: The tree follows SpectraLab's stated purpose closely: photo → peaks → wavelength calibration → element ranking → grating constant with uncertainty → export and report, plus the validation bench. The labels are clean, and every screen I checked shows what its node says. Before filing, it needs small structural fixes: fold the one-click 'clear calibration' task into calibration, add a 'judge fit quality' step, and record the element-ID threshold and the fact that identification was only tested on synthetic data.
